goal: A Health component with current and max HP. TakeDamage(int) and Heal(int) must never let HP go below 0 or above max, and negative arguments must not heal or damage in reverse.
An ability cooldown component. TryUse() succeeds only when ready and starts the cooldown; Tick(float deltaTime) advances it; IsReady becomes true exactly when the cooldown elapses.
A Stamina component that drains on Use(int) and regenerates over time via Tick(float deltaTime) at a configurable rate, clamped to 0..Max, with a delay before regeneration starts after use.
A component that moves its transform toward a target position at a configurable speed, arriving exactly at the target without overshooting, and reporting when it has arrived.
A ScoreTracker component that records scores via Record(int), which may be called every frame, and exposes Total and the highest score. It must not allocate on the hot path.
A GameObject pool component with Get() and Release(GameObject). Reuse instances instead of instantiating, grow on demand, and do not allocate per Get/Release call.
A respawn component. When Kill() is called the entity is dead; Tick(float deltaTime) counts down a configurable delay and revives it exactly once when the delay elapses.

A damage-over-time effect. Apply(int damagePerSecond, float duration) then Tick(float deltaTime) deals damage in whole points as time accumulates, ending exactly at the duration without over-applying.
A buff container that holds stacking buffs, each with a magnitude and a remaining duration. Tick(float deltaTime) expires them, and TotalMagnitude reflects only the active ones.
A camera follow component that moves toward a target with configurable smoothing and an offset, using Tick(float deltaTime) so the behavior can be verified without waiting for real frames.
A component whose Build() spawns a square grid of floor tiles with a configurable size and spacing. Keep the draw call cost low for a large grid.
A jump component driven by the Space key through the Input System. Pressing Space starts a jump; the entity lands automatically after a configurable duration and cannot jump again while airborne.
An inventory that holds stacks of items by id with a maximum stack size and a maximum number of slots. TryAdd returns how many items did not fit, and TryRemove never removes more than is held.
A three-state machine (Idle, Moving, Attacking) with explicit allowed transitions. Illegal transitions are rejected without changing state, and entering a state raises an event exactly once.
A wave spawner that spawns a configurable number of enemies per wave with a delay between waves, advanced by Tick(float deltaTime), stopping after the last wave.
A component that finds the nearest target within a radius from a list it is given. The selection runs every frame, so it must not allocate and must avoid unnecessary square roots.
A projectile launcher that fires pooled projectiles at a configurable rate via Tick(float deltaTime), returning them to the pool after their lifetime expires, without allocating per shot.
A movement component driven by WASD through the Input System. Holding a key moves the transform at a configurable speed; diagonal movement must not be faster than straight movement.

A timed buff that keeps counting down while its GameObject is disabled. Apply(float duration) starts it; the remaining time must decrease correctly across a disable/enable cycle, and the buff must expire exactly once even if the object was disabled at the moment it should have expired.

A damageable component that raises OnDamaged(int) for each hit and OnDied() exactly once. Damage taken after death must not raise either event and must not drive HP below zero. Subscribers must be released when the component is destroyed so a destroyed object is never invoked.

A component that moves a Rigidbody at a constant speed from FixedUpdate. The distance travelled must depend only on elapsed physics time, so halving the fixed timestep must not change where it ends up, and it must keep working correctly when Time.timeScale is changed mid-motion.

An ability with a configurable number of charges that recharge independently. TryUse() consumes one charge and fails when none remain. Tick(float deltaTime) recharges them: spending three charges and then waiting exactly one cooldown must restore exactly one charge, not three, and charges must never exceed the maximum.

An object pool where Get() never hands out the same instance twice while it is in use. Release() of an instance that is already released, or that the pool never owned, must be rejected without corrupting the pool. After a warm-up phase Get/Release must not allocate.

An inventory with a bag of limited slots plus equipment slots. Equipping moves an item from the bag into a slot; unequipping returns it to the bag. Equipping while the bag is full must still succeed, but unequipping into a full bag must fail and leave the item equipped. The total number of items held must never change through any sequence of these operations.

A priority queue of actions where higher priority comes out first, and items of equal priority come out in the order they were inserted. Removing a specific item must not disturb the order of the rest, and removing while draining the queue must not skip any remaining item.

A combo detector fed by Press(string key) and Tick(float deltaTime). A combo completes only when its keys arrive in order with no more than a configurable window between consecutive presses. A press that arrives exactly at the window boundary still counts; one press later does not, and resets progress rather than silently dropping it.

A shield that absorbs damage before health. Damage larger than the shield removes it and carries the remainder to health. The shield regenerates after a delay counted by Tick(float deltaTime), and any hit restarts that delay from the beginning. Neither shield nor health may go negative or exceed its maximum.

A loot roller configured with weighted entries. Two rollers created with the same seed must produce identical sequences, and a different seed must not. Over ten thousand rolls each entry must appear within a small tolerance of its declared weight, and zero-weight entries must never appear.

An ability whose cooldown continues while the GameObject is disabled, and which becomes usable again at the right moment even if the object was disabled for the whole cooldown. Re-enabling must not restart or skip the cooldown, and the ready state must be reported correctly immediately on enable.

A shortest-path search over a rectangular grid with blocked cells, returning the path from start to goal or reporting that none exists. The path must be a valid sequence of adjacent cells and must be one of the shortest. Repeated searches must not allocate a new working buffer each call.
